title: Ring objects of abelian sheaves
statement:
A *ring object* of a monoidal category $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1)$ is a monoid
object. It consists of an object $R$, a *multiplication* $\mu\colon R\otimes R\to R$ and
a *unit* $\eta\colon\mathbf 1\to R$, such that $\mu$ is associative,
$\mu\circ(\mu\otimes\mathrm{id})=\mu\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mu)\circ\alpha_{R,R,R}$, and
$\eta$ is a two-sided unit, $\mu\circ(\eta\otimes\mathrm{id})=\lambda_R$ and
$\mu\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes\eta)=\rho_R$. A *morphism of ring objects* is a morphism
compatible with the multiplications and the units. If $\mathcal C$ is braided, the ring
object $R$ is *commutative* when $\mu\circ\beta_{R,R}=\mu$.

Throughout, $\Ab$ carries the tensor product $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ with unit $\mathbf Z$.
Abelian presheaves carry the objectwise tensor product. Abelian sheaves on a site $C$
carry its sheafification, the tensor product of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] (with $C$ as
there, e.g. $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ or the site of profinite sets).

1. Every ring $R$ is a ring object of $\Ab$, with unit $\mathbf Z\to R$, $n\mapsto n\cdot1$,
   and multiplication $R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R\to R$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. A ring
   homomorphism is a morphism of ring objects. If $R$ is commutative, so is the ring
   object $R$.
2. A presheaf of rings $P$ on $C$ is, objectwise as in 1, a ring object of abelian
   presheaves, and a morphism of presheaves of rings is a morphism of ring objects. The
   sheafification $aP$ of the underlying abelian presheaf is a ring object of
   $\Sh(C,\Ab)$, commutative when all the rings $P(U)$ are.
3. The abelian sheaf underlying a sheaf of rings $\mathcal R$ on $C$ is a ring object of
   $\Sh(C,\Ab)$, commutative when all the rings $\mathcal R(U)$ are. A morphism of sheaves
   of rings is a morphism of ring objects.

proof.text: Ring objects, their morphisms, and braided commutativity are exactly the monoid-object clauses in [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]. The ordinary-ring realization and ring-homomorphism and commutativity claims are [det-def-sfb-ring-object-rings]. The presheaf realization and its sheafification are [det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf], and the underlying sheaf-of-rings realization and morphism claim are [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf]. These four nodes are stated for the monoidal structure of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] on $\Sh(C,\Ab)$, for a site $C$ with essentially small underlying category and $\Ab$ with $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and unit $\mathbf Z$; this is the item's convention. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], part (2), for $\mathcal A=\Ab$ (Grothendieck abelian, closed symmetric monoidal, $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ additive in each variable) on the same kind of site gives the tensor product $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G=a(\iota\mathcal F\otimes_p\iota\mathcal G)$ with unit $a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$, for which $a$ is strong symmetric monoidal. These are the tensor product, unit and strong symmetric monoidal sheafification of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], whose associator, unitors and symmetry are $a$ of the objectwise ones transported along the comparison isomorphisms $aP\otimes aQ\cong a(P\otimes_pQ)$. Since every sheaf $\mathcal F$ is $a(\iota\mathcal F)$ through the counit, the coherence isomorphisms are determined by these comparisons, so both nodes describe the same symmetric monoidal category. Hence the ring objects, morphisms and commutativity in the four detail nodes are those of the item, and combining them gives all three clauses.
